23 A source of sound of frequency 1000 Hz moves away from a stationary observer at a speed of
30.0 m s–1. The speed of sound is 330 m s–1.
What is the frequency of the sound heard by the observer?
A
909 Hz
B
917 Hz
C
1090 Hz
D
1100 Hz

hints: Notice the source moves away from a stationary observer, so successive wavefronts are stretched out and the observed wavelength is longer than the emitted wavelength.
Recall the Doppler formula for a receding source: $f_o = f_s v/(v + v_s)$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s = 30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate $330/(330+30)$ times $1000 \text{ Hz}$ and check that your answer is slightly below $1000 \text{ Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify the situation: source frequency $f_s = 1000 \text{ Hz}$, source speed $v_s = 30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away from observer, wave speed $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, observer stationary.
State the rule: a receding source increases the observed wavelength to $\lambda_o = (v + v_s)/f_s$, so observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s v/(v + v_s)$ is reduced.
Calculate the intermediate ratio: $330/360 = 0.9167$, so $f_o = 1000 \times 0.9167 = 916.7 \text{ Hz}$.
Round sensibly to $917 \text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$, which is lower than $1000 \text{ Hz}$ as expected for recession. This is option B.

A.explanation: This uses $f_o = f_s(v - v_s)/v$ which applies to a moving observer, not a receding source, giving $1000 \times 300/330 \approx 909 \text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: For a source receding at $30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $f_o = f_s v/(v+v_s) \approx 917 \text{ Hz}$, so observed frequency is lower.

C.explanation: This is greater than $1000 \text{ Hz}$, which would require an approaching source to shorten the observed wavelength.

D.explanation: This adds the speed ratio directly as $1000 \times (360/330)$, giving a higher frequency instead of the lower frequency for recession.
